text: In these five leaves one side's ko capture is not atari, so the other side can ignore it once: the capturer must first fill a liberty, and only then is the ko direct. That fill is the approach move: White 8 in Diagram 1, Black 9 in Diagram 2 and White 13 in Diagram 3. The leaves in 1807 and 14153 work like Diagram 1. All five trees say S[KO+], which leaves the approach move out. The analysis and both reviewers found that wrong in every leaf; the question is only how to write the right label.

The analysis and one reviewer of each leaf write the counted label, which counts the approach move as one more threat. In Diagram 1 White must win the ko twice, with White 6 and White 10: S[KO+2]. In Diagram 2 White 10 retakes for free, so Black, the player, must find the first threat: S[KO-]. In Diagram 3 White, the player, must win the ko twice, with White 11 and White 15: S[KO-2]. The site's tutorial calls S[KO+2] and S[KO-2] a two-step ko.

The other reviewer writes besogo's approach-ko label, which keeps the approach move out of the threats and says who took the ko first. In Diagram 1 the opponent needs one approach move, White 8, and the player took first with Black 5: S[A+1KO+]. In Diagram 2 the player needs it, Black 9, and took first with Black 7: S[A-1KO+]. In Diagram 3 the player needs it, White 13, and the opponent took first with Black 10: S[A-1KO-].

Both labels need exactly the same threats, so the checker accepts either. besogo ranks them differently, because it compares approach moves before threats: for the player, S[A+1KO+] is better than every ko label without approach moves, and S[A-1KO+] and S[A-1KO-] are worse than all of them. In these five problems that changes nothing: neither label changes which moves the site marks correct, nor any problem's result. The site already writes these shapes with approach-ko labels, in 2521, 15418, 215, 10391 and 7487.

diagrams.caption: 10974, Black to live. The tree's line ends with Black 5 taking the ko, marked S[KO+]; a leaf of problem 2521 with the same position is marked S[A+1KO+]. White 6 retakes after a threat, but Black still has two liberties and plays elsewhere with Black 7. White 8 fills one, and Black 9 retakes without a threat. Only a second threat lets White 10 retake; with no threat left, Black dies.

5628, Black to kill. The tree's line ends with White 6, marked S[KO+]. Black 7 takes the ko first, but White still has a liberty at E16, so the capture is no atari and White plays elsewhere with White 8. Black 9 has to fill E16, and White 10 retakes without a threat. Now Black, with four stones in atari, must find the first threat.

suggestion: The approach-ko labels, as besogo describes these shapes and as the site already writes them. If you choose them, I can check the other KO+2 and KO−2 fixes in this report for the same shape; their reviewers did not raise it.
